limitations: Historical Linux execution record, not a rerun or independent attestation; tools/verify-validation.py checks source binding, not original log contents or execution.
Windows and macOS native linking, runtime, packaging and Shell/Finder integration remain unverified; docs/windows-validation.md is an unexecuted manual procedure.
Current-source COFF x86_64 and Mach-O aarch64 object emission passed. Intel Mach-O x86_64 emission still fails on unsupported plt32 relocation; object emission is not runtime support.

External file-list paste and inbound multiple-file/directory/symlink drag and drop are COPY-only. Internal Cut requires the still-owned clipboard provider/generation; cross-process external Cut is not promised.
GTK synchronous drop acceptance means accepted/queued. Owned paths and context survive until the engine result; the drag source receives no asynchronous filesystem-completion result.

GTK/X11 cancellation completion can wait for an unresponsive external clipboard owner. The request stays pending and context stays alive until the real callback, without a false acknowledgement or filesystem mutation.

The partial-Cut completion acceptance is an AOT unit using actual helpers and real providers with constructed per-item outcomes, including generation replacement before a real asynchronous callback; it is not a partial-filesystem-failure end-to-end test.

Folder filtering is literal case-folded current-directory filename matching, not recursive or indexed search. Native shell-extension menus, ACL editing, recycle-bin browsing, archives and operation undo remain separate work.
Move has no copy/delete fallback; failed or cancelled copies may retain explicitly reported partial destinations. Existing targets are not replaced or merged.

The former directory-DND rejection test was replaced by real nested directory COPY and collision preservation. Existing file COPY now waits for actual final completion before collision retry; other substantive legacy assertions are retained.
